name: Question 20
worked_solution:
The cross-product rule states that

$$
{\int }_{1}^{5}c\times f(t)\,\text{d}t=c\times {\int }_{1}^{5}f(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

 

Applying the cross-product rule, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{5}c\times f(t)\,\text{d}t & =c\times {\int }_{1}^{5}f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =(2\,i-k)\times (i-j+3\,k) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 0 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}|k \\  & =(0-1)i-(6+1)j+(-2-0)k \\  & =-i-7\,j-2\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 20

Find ∫15c×f(t)dt given that ∫15f(t)dt=i−j+3k and c=2i−k.

a
2i+7j−k
b
−2i+7j−4k
c
−i+2j−3k
d
2i+4j−2k
e
−i−7j−2k
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The cross-product rule states that

∫15c×f(t)dt=c×∫15f(t)dt.

Applying the cross-product rule, we have

∫15c×f(t)dt=c×∫15f(t)dt=(2i−k)×(i−j+3k)=|ijk20−11−13|=|0−1−13|i−|2−113|j+|201−1|k=(0−1)i−(6+1)j+(−2−0)k=−i−7j−2k.
